answer: In an agent marketplace trading willow, timber, and walnut, each identity must lock 100 tokens in escrow for 30 days before it can submit bids, and the same deposit cannot back two identities. An attacker operating 1,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize 100,000 tokens for a month, paying financing costs or forgoing other uses of that capital. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes multiplying active identities expensive.
